alerts.title: Acute Kidney Injury with TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines list TDF as a cause of acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease. The patient has an acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, up from 0.9 mg/dL) with dehydration from severe gastroenteritis. Evidence for TDF attribution includes the known toxicity. Evidence against includes a clear non-drug cause (dehydration from gastroenteritis) and a high urea-to-creatinine ratio (24:1) suggestive of pre-renal azotemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Do LFTs and RFTs. If deranged, manage per toxicity guidelines.

alerts.title: TDF Contraindication in Kidney Disease
alerts.message: Guidelines state TDF is contraindicated in kidney disease with eGFR below 60 ml/min. The patient's acute kidney injury likely corresponds to an eGFR below 60 ml/min, creating a contraindication. The clinician's plan to consider stopping TDF permanently aligns with this guideline.

evidence.recommended_action: Substitute TDF with an alternative regimen, such as ABC+3TC+DTG, as TDF is contraindicated.

alerts.title: Missing TDF Renal Monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The patient has been on TDF for 2 years, and the last recorded creatinine was 375 days ago. This gap exceeds the 12-month monitoring interval.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform serum creatinine and eGFR as per the 12-month monitoring schedule for patients on TDF.

alerts.title: Hypokalemia Risk with TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines list exhaustion, extreme fatigue, and muscle cramps as presenting signs for TDF toxicity, which can be associated with electrolyte disturbances like hypokalemia. The patient has hypokalemia (potassium 3.1 mmol/L) and symptoms of dizziness and fatigue from dehydration. This electrolyte abnormality compounds the risk in the setting of acute kidney injury.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor potassium closely and correct hypokalemia, especially in the context of kidney injury.
